updates.subject: Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review
updates.changed_content:
Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review

This section establishes the shared considerations for qualifying for, maintaining and reviewing compensation levels. The employee’s completed individual schedule identifies the assigned category, level and rates. These expectations take effect prospectively under the employee’s amendment and written notice; they do not create undisclosed retroactive criteria.

Annual paid event-work commitment

I agree to participate in a minimum of four (4) hours of assigned outreach or agency events during each calendar year, January 1 through December 31, compensated separately at my agreed-upon indirect hourly rate. Actual event time is recorded and paid separately from service-credit compensation and automatic H-code indirect allowances; the same work may not be counted or paid twice.

Next Level Up and the employee will identify and schedule the indirect duties that satisfy this commitment, including assigned outreach, community events. Required outreach under this commitment is paid indirect work, not unpaid volunteering. Other activities retain the pay classification disclosed in the compensation schedule unless expressly designated as part of this indirect-work assignment. The commitment does not automatically add four hours to payroll: record all actual time worked, including additional compensable time. Next Level Up will make assignments and scheduling expectations clear. Management will address unavailable assignments, center closures, approved schedule changes, protected leave and reasonable accommodations; an employee will not be treated as failing this commitment solely because Next Level Up did not make the work available. Requirements are adjusted as required for protected leave and accommodations, without unpaid make-up work. Applicable minimum wage and overtime protections continue to apply.

Evaluation categories

1. Annual paid event-work commitment

Complete the assigned four-hour annual event commitment (January 1–December 31), with accurate actual-time records and timely follow-through. Review both the work made available and the work performed; do not substitute automatic payroll allowances for actual participation.

Review evidence: Assigned duties, agreed schedules, time records and completed work, with approved adjustments documented.

2. Documentation quality and timeliness

Complete accurate notes, treatment plans and required documentation within the communicated clinical, payer and agency deadlines. Correct errors and respond to documentation requests promptly. Review system outages, approved extensions and protected absences before identifying a performance concern.

Review evidence: Applicable deadlines, completion records, accuracy reviews and the employee’s explanation of barriers.

3. Attendance, call-offs and clinician cancellations

Meet agreed schedules, give timely notice when unable to attend, and support appropriate client notification, rescheduling and coverage. Consider avoidable clinician cancellations and unprotected attendance concerns in context. Exclude protected leave and accommodations; distinguish clinician decisions from client cancellations, center closures and events outside the employee’s control.

Review evidence: Scheduling and notice records, reasons for cancellations, coverage efforts and confirmed circumstances.

4. Outreach and team participation

Participate in assigned outreach events and practice partnership activities that fit the employee’s role and disclosed schedule. Communicate conflicts and complete agreed alternatives when appropriate. Assigned outreach hours under this commitment are paid at the agreed indirect rate and count toward the four-hour calendar-year total; additional actual work remains compensable.

Review evidence: Event assignments, participation, completed follow-up and documented scheduling arrangements.

5. Professional standing, collaboration and feedback

Maintain required credentials and supervision, follow professional and agency standards, communicate respectfully and address substantiated concerns. Consider reports from clients, families and staff after reviewing facts, context and the employee’s response. A complaint alone is not a finding of misconduct or an automatic basis for a lower level. Good-faith reporting, wage concerns and other protected activity are not adverse factors.

Review evidence: Credential and supervision records, specific observed conduct, documented feedback and reviewed findings.

6. Client connection and engagement

Build a responsive, respectful therapeutic relationship; communicate appropriately with clients and authorized caregivers; and address access, language and engagement barriers within the employee’s role. Evaluate the clinician’s actions and quality of care, with attention to client choice and confidentiality, rather than popularity or retention alone.

Review evidence: Appropriate feedback, communication and follow-up records, care coordination and documented engagement efforts.

7. Treatment goals, progress and appropriate completion of care

Develop individualized goals and objectives, assess progress, adjust care when needed, and support clinically appropriate goal attainment, termination, transfer or referral. Consider client acuity, readiness, disability, learning context and other barriers. Progress is a consideration, not a guaranteed outcome. Do not reward unnecessary treatment, premature discharge, selecting only easier cases or a predetermined number of successful terminations.

Review evidence: Clinical review of treatment planning, progress assessment, appropriate adjustments and continuity-of-care decisions.

8. Client and program action items

Complete assigned intake, family contact, program coordination, roster, scheduling and other client action items by communicated deadlines. Keep status records accurate and escalate blocked items promptly. Apply role-specific responsibilities within authorized information-sharing boundaries.

Review evidence: Task assignments, due dates, completion records, escalations and documented external dependencies.

Evaluation schedule and good standing

Next Level Up will conduct formal compensation-level evaluations one to two times per year. Supervisors may provide feedback and address concerns between formal evaluations. Reviews consider the responsibilities applicable to the employee’s role, the expectations disclosed in advance, reliable evidence and the employee’s response. Good standing means substantially meeting the applicable professional, documentation, reliability, participation and follow-through expectations, with concerns assessed fairly and in context. Protected leave, reasonable accommodations and other protected activity are excluded from adverse consideration.

For each applicable category, document “Meets expectations,” “Needs improvement” or “Not applicable,” with the review period, supporting facts and the employee’s comments. Disclose role- or level-specific standards before using them. This framework does not establish undisclosed point totals, weighting or automatic promotion/demotion thresholds.

Maintaining or changing a compensation level

A review may result in maintaining the current compensation level, advancement when the applicable criteria are met, or a prospective reduction within the employee’s compensation category when documented expectations are not met. Advancement is not automatic. Management will communicate the reasons, relevant evidence and expectations for improvement, ordinarily with a written improvement plan and a follow-up date; serious concerns may require earlier action. The employee may submit a response or request management review. Any changed level and resulting rates must be communicated in writing before affected work, with any agreement required by existing terms. No review reduces pay or leave already earned. A handbook edit, complaint, missed task or app-generated flag does not automatically change an employee’s pay level. Credential categories and session-based workload tiers remain distinct from performance-based compensation levels; Tier 3 bonus eligibility continues to follow the disclosed session-count rules.

Clinical decisions must prioritize appropriate care and client choice. Reviewers must not use treatment outcomes or discharge counts as quotas. Share only the information appropriate for the review; detailed clinical records remain in the authorized clinical record.

Supervisory review and evaluations

Supervisory reviews, clinical documentation reviews and formal performance evaluations are also considered when determining whether an employee meets the expectations for their compensation level. Findings must be documented, reviewed in context and discussed with the employee.

GENERAL ATTENDANCE GUIDELINES

Professionalism and Reliability:

All employees and contractors, regardless of their employment status, are expected to maintain a high level of professionalism, which includes being reliable and punctual.

Communication:

Prompt communication in case of any anticipated tardiness or absence is crucial. This helps in maintaining transparency and allows for any necessary adjustments to be made.

Documentation:

Document attendance, tardiness and leave through the designated channels. Performance reviews consider unprotected attendance concerns in context and exclude protected leave and reasonable accommodations, as described in Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review.

Accountability:

Employees and contractors are accountable for meeting their agreed schedules. Repeated unexplained, unprotected absences or tardiness may result in corrective action, up to and including termination of employment or contract. Review the circumstances and the person’s response before deciding on action; protected leave and accommodations are excluded from adverse consideration.

Support and Resources

We acknowledge that various circumstances can affect attendance. Employees and contractors are encouraged to communicate openly with their supervisors or People Operations department if they are experiencing challenges that could impact their attendance.

The organization is committed to providing support and resources to address these challenges and foster a positive and reliable work environment.

Continuity of Care Policy

To ensure that clients receive consistent and reliable support, the following guidelines apply:

If an employee is unable to meet with a client for three (3) consecutive scheduled sessions or is unavailable to meet with the client for a period of three to four (3–4) weeks for any reason, the client will be reassigned to another employee who has availability.

This policy is in place to protect client progress and therapeutic continuity.

Reassignment decisions will be handled by the supervisor or program director to ensure a smooth transition for the client.

Non-Mandatory Company Events

Purpose: Team-building and culture activities (e.g., outings, social gatherings).

Attendance: Voluntary, not a work-related obligation.

Compensation: Attendance at a truly optional social event is on the employee’s own time. Assigned outreach, agency event work follows the paid four-hour annual commitment, in Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review. Record and pay actual assigned work separately, including additional compensable time.

Encouragement: Participation is encouraged as part of building a positive workplace culture.

PERFORMANCE AND EXPECTATIONS

This section outlines professional, clinical, billing, and compliance expectations applicable to all employees providing services on behalf of Next Level Up. Failure to meet these expectations may result in corrective action in accordance with Practice policies.

Clinical Service Standards

A Clinical Session or Clinical Service is considered properly rendered only when:

  • The service is actually delivered;
  • The service is within the employee’s scope of practice, training, and credentialing;
  • Required authorizations are obtained when applicable; and
  • Clinical documentation is completed in accordance with Practice standards.

Administrative, concierge, subscription, or other payments to Next Level Up do not create an automatic employee revenue share. Employees are paid for the services and assigned duties they actually perform under their individual compensation schedule and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION. Required administrative work remains compensable under Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Documentation Standards

Timely, accurate, and complete clinical documentation is a fundamental professional responsibility.

Documentation must be completed in accordance with Practice standards and applicable laws.

Documentation that is late, incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent with services rendered may render a service Deficient.

Documentation timeliness and payroll deadlines follow TIMEKEEPING, COMPENSATION, AND PAYROLL COMPLIANCE. Documentation and approval concerns are handled separately from paying for work performed.

Deficient Services

Deficient Services include, but are not limited to, services that:

  • Are not delivered as scheduled or documented as delivered;
  • Are inadequately, inaccurately, or untimely documented;
  • Are provided in violation of third-party payor rules, applicable laws, or ethical standards;
  • Are conducted outside of required licensure, credentialing, or authorization parameters; or
  • Result in denial, recoupment, or retraction of payment due to provider-controlled noncompliance.

Deficient Services may result in corrective action, remediation, review of billing privileges, client reassignment, or other appropriate compliance action. Correct inaccurate records and payment errors through the designated review process. A late note, missing preapproval, or denied claim does not erase earned wages; Actual time, support activities and corrections governs compensation for actual work.

Billing and Insurance Compliance

Employees are responsible for complying with all billing, insurance, and payor requirements applicable to the services they provide.

Credentialing and Licensure

Employees must maintain required licensure and credentialing to bill insurance.

Delays or failures attributable to the employee that prevent insurance billing may result in client transition to self-pay or reassignment.

The Practice reserves the right to inform clients of credentialing limitations impacting billing.

Insurance Denials and Recoupment

If a payer denies or retracts payment because of inadequate services or documentation, address the billing and compliance issue through review and correction. A payer denial does not automatically deny, reduce, or recoup employee compensation already earned. Apply Actual time, support activities and corrections and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION.

Repeated billing deficiencies may result in loss of insurance billing privileges.

Medicaid-Specific Rules

Medicaid clients may never be charged self-pay rates.

If a provider is unable to bill Medicaid due to noncompliance, services must be provided pro-bono or clients must be transferred for continuity of care.

Providers who fall out of compliance may be restricted or revoked from serving Medicaid clients until compliance is restored.

Self-Pay Services

Clients who are uninsured, elect not to use insurance, receive services not covered by insurance, or lack a billable diagnosis may be billed at self-pay rates in accordance with Practice policy.

All self-pay clients are billed at Practice minimum rates unless otherwise approved.

Required self-pay and No Surprises Act forms must be completed prior to billing.

Non-billable diagnoses must be handled as self-pay unless otherwise specified by policy.

Reduced Rates (Sliding Scale)

Reduced rates may be approved on a case-by-case basis to support access to care.

Requests must be initiated through the Support Team and approved by appropriate leadership.

Reduced rates must be client-initiated due to financial hardship and must contribute meaningfully to care (e.g., increased frequency or duration).

An approved reduction in a client’s rate does not automatically reduce the employee’s compensation. Covered services and duties use the individual compensation schedule under COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION; changes apply prospectively with the required notice and agreement.

Reduced rates most commonly apply to 90837 services, with approved rates set by policy.

Billing protocols must be followed as outlined by the Administrative Team.

Pro-Bono Services

Pro-bono services may be approved to support clients experiencing financial hardship.

Approval must be obtained prior to initiation.

Pro-bono describes the charge to the client. Approved work performed by an employee remains compensated under the applicable individual service or duty rate and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION. No client charge or reimbursement does not make compensable employee work unpaid.

Pro-bono services may apply to any service offered by the provider.

Sessions must be properly identified and documented in the app in accordance with Practice protocols.

Professional Conduct and Ethics

Employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of professional and ethical conduct, including compliance with:

  • The ACA Code of Ethics;
  • HIPAA and confidentiality requirements; and
  • All applicable laws and regulations.

Ethical or legal concerns must be reported promptly to Compliance. Failure to report or address known concerns may result in corrective action.

Auditing and Oversight

Next Level Up conducts periodic review and auditing of clinical documentation and services, including through third-party compliance partners.

Findings of significant noncompliance or unethical conduct may result in remediation, corrective action, or further disciplinary measures as outlined in the Remediation section of this Handbook.

EMPLOYEE SEPARATION AND TRANSITIONS RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION

Voluntary Terminations:

A voluntary termination occurs when an employee gives notice of resignation. Three consecutive workdays without contact may prompt a job-abandonment review. Before treating the absence as resignation, review the circumstances, available notice, protected leave, and reasonable accommodations under Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review.

Procedures:
  1. Employees are requested to provide a minimum of two weeks' notice of their intention to separate from Next Level Up to allow a reasonable amount of time to transfer ongoing workloads. The employee should submit a written resignation notification to the manager through the app.
  2. Upon receipt of an employee's resignation, the manager will notify the People Operations (PO) department by submitting the resignation record and relevant details, including the reason for leaving and last day of work, through the app.
  3. The PO department will coordinate the employee's out-processing. This process will include the employee's returning all company property (computers, documentation, keys, etc.); a review of the employee's post termination benefits status; and the employee's completion of an exit interview.
  4. The employee's manager will complete and submit the Supervisory Termination Summary to People Operations in the app.
  5. Employees who possess a security clearance (security codes to the building, computer passwords, etc.) must meet with administration for a debriefing no later than their last day of employment.
  6. Employees are required to provide management with the caseload handoff in the app and cannot take their clients with them according to the employee and company’s non-compete agreement.

Involuntary Terminations:

An involuntary termination of employment, including layoffs of over 30 days, is a management-initiated dismissal with or without cause. The inability of an employee to perform the essential functions of his or her job with or without a reasonable accommodation may also result in an involuntary termination. An employee may also be discharged for any legal reason, including but not limited to: misconduct, tardiness, absenteeism, unsatisfactory performance, inability to perform.

Procedures:
  1. Before any action is taken to involuntarily discharge an employee, the employee's manager must request a review by PO and the employee's immediate supervisor.
  2. The termination review staff will be responsible for reviewing the circumstances and determining if discharge is warranted. If the staff recommends discharge, the employee's manager and a PO representative will notify the employee. The employee's manager should complete the Employee Change Form in the app and notify People Operations and Payroll through the app of the last day worked.

Final Pay:

An employee who resigns or is discharged will be paid through the last day of work, plus any unused paid time off (PTO) under the Termination Payout provisions of the leave policy, less outstanding loans, advances or other agreements the employee may have with Next Level Up, in compliance with state laws.

Death of an Employee:

A termination due to the death of an employee will be made effective as of the date of death.

Procedures:
  1. Upon receiving notification of the death of an employee, the employee's manager should immediately notify PO.
  2. The benefits administrator will process all appropriate beneficiary payments from the various benefits plans.
  3. The employee's manager should ensure that Payroll can review the deceased employee’s completed time records in the app.

updates.subject: Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff
updates.changed_content:
Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff

Initial ratio: 20% administrative equivalent

Clinical credits × 1.20 ÷ 30 = sick-leave hours earned. The direct bucket receives 1.00 equivalent hour per credit and the administrative bucket receives 0.20. Thus 25 credits = 30 equivalent hours = 1 hour of sick leave; 0.75 credit = 0.90 equivalent hour = 0.03 sick-leave hour. The administrative equivalent affects accrual only for psychotherapy credit services and is already included in service pay.

Integrated Direct Service time and its included Indirect Service time enter the accrual calculation once. Under the standard 20% allowance, one direct hour plus 0.20 included indirect hour equals 1.20 accrual hours. Do not apply another clinical-credit multiplier to that total. Separately compensated Indirect Service, Support Activity, and qualifying Excess Time also count without duplication. Reconcile against all actual compensable work and apply any required sick-leave shortfall.

This remains protected paid sick leave, not a new vacation bank. It accrues without a probation waiting period and is paid using the highest currently eligible rate under the sick-leave pay policy. Payroll applies the HFWA calculation rules for the leave dates, using the currently applicable clinical per-credit or direct hourly base rate, excluding Tier 3 additions and other bonuses or differentials. Preserve existing balances and more generous earned terms. HFWA generally requires at least one hour per 30 hours worked up to 48 annually, with applicable carryover up to 48 hours; protected uses, reasonable notice, permitted documentation and nonretaliation requirements apply. Do not apply a generic 10-hour rollover cap or 30-day notice rule to protected sick leave.

Next Level Up may update the ratio prospectively through the dated handbook appendix and corresponding payroll policy version, with notice and any required agreement. Preserve accrued balances and historical service calculations. AI documentation does not change the ratio automatically or remove pay for required review and correction. Actual work remains compensable even with a zero allowance. Any separate vacation/general PTO entitlement retains its existing protections.

GENERAL ATTENDANCE GUIDELINES

Professionalism and Reliability:

All employees and contractors, regardless of their employment status, are expected to maintain a high level of professionalism, which includes being reliable and punctual.

Communication:

Prompt communication in case of any anticipated tardiness or absence is crucial. This helps in maintaining transparency and allows for any necessary adjustments to be made.

Documentation:

Document attendance, tardiness and leave through the designated channels. Performance reviews consider unprotected attendance concerns in context and exclude protected leave and reasonable accommodations, as described in Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review.

Accountability:

Employees and contractors are accountable for meeting their agreed schedules. Repeated unexplained, unprotected absences or tardiness may result in corrective action, up to and including termination of employment or contract. Review the circumstances and the person’s response before deciding on action; protected leave and accommodations are excluded from adverse consideration.

Support and Resources

We acknowledge that various circumstances can affect attendance. Employees and contractors are encouraged to communicate openly with their supervisors or People Operations department if they are experiencing challenges that could impact their attendance.

The organization is committed to providing support and resources to address these challenges and foster a positive and reliable work environment.

Continuity of Care Policy

To ensure that clients receive consistent and reliable support, the following guidelines apply:

If an employee is unable to meet with a client for three (3) consecutive scheduled sessions or is unavailable to meet with the client for a period of three to four (3–4) weeks for any reason, the client will be reassigned to another employee who has availability.

This policy is in place to protect client progress and therapeutic continuity.

Reassignment decisions will be handled by the supervisor or program director to ensure a smooth transition for the client.

Attendance Guidelines for Non-Provider/Facilitator Employees

Work Hours:

Salaried, full-time, and part-time employees are expected to fulfill their roles and responsibilities as outlined in their employment contracts. While some roles may offer flexibility, adherence to core working hours is required unless otherwise agreed upon with management.

Reporting Absences:

Employees must notify their direct supervisor or designated point of contact as soon as possible in case of any unplanned absence.

Planned Leaves:

Request foreseeable planned leave through the applicable leave process. Protected sick leave follows Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff, including its reasonable-notice provisions; a general advance-approval rule does not override protected leave.

updates.subject: Actual time, support activities and corrections
updates.changed_content:
Actual time, support activities and corrections

The Workplace Handbook identifies activities eligible for indirect pay and support-activity pay. These activity types will be added to the web application as needed. Next Level Up reserves the right to designate activities as indirect work or support activities and to add, revise or reclassify activity types prospectively. The applicable classification and rate will be communicated before the work is performed. Record actual compensable time under the designated activity; a missing app option should be reported for entry or correction. A later classification change does not reduce pay already earned or permit duplicate payment.

Record all compensable work daily. Provider Update active review time is tracked by session and section and submitted for payroll review at the applicable support activity rate. Paused, hidden and timed-out periods are not automatically credited; report legitimate unrecorded work through a correction request. Actual work beyond an allowance remains compensable.

Clinical credits and automatic indirect equivalents are not substitutes for actual time records. Apply applicable minimum wage, overtime, rest-period and regular-rate rules, including workweek and daily requirements. A late note, missing preapproval or denied claim does not erase earned wages. Handle documentation or approval concerns separately from paying for work performed.

Clinical supervision compensation

Clinical supervision is paid at the supervisor’s individually negotiated or contracted hourly rate. This handbook does not set a universal supervision dollar rate.

Assigned responsibilityCompensation basis
Direct clinical supervision100% of the contracted supervision hourly rate
Hosting group clinical supervision150% of the contracted supervision hourly rate
Reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes50% of the contracted supervision hourly rate per actual note-review hour

Group pay is based on actual hosting time, not the number of participants. Note-review pay covers actual time reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes, not the supervisor’s own notes. Record review time separately without duplicate payment or an automatic allowance per supervision hour. Paused and inactive time is excluded from automatic tracking; report legitimate work the tracker misses for correction. Tracked time remains under payroll review until accepted and applied. The supervisor’s individual agreement identifies their contracted rate.

ORGANIZATIONAL MEETINGS POLICY

Organizational meetings are a core part of maintaining communication, collaboration, and alignment across the Practice. Attendance and participation in required meetings are considered part of each employee’s work responsibilities and are compensable.

Recording & Compensation of Meetings

Time submission: Record actual compensable meeting time in the designated app and payroll workflow as Support Activity, unless a separately assigned duty and rate apply. General staff, administrative, evaluation, leadership, and operational meetings are not automatically client-related Indirect Service. See 14. Support Activity and Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Identify the meeting by its name, date and purpose in the app’s activity record. Follow App records, forms and timekeeping for app records and timekeeping.

Duration: Meeting time should be entered for the actual minutes attended.

Compensation:

If a contract lists a “meeting rate”, including but not limited to administrative meeting, training meeting, etc., that rate will apply.

If no separately agreed meeting or duty rate applies, use the employee’s applicable Support Activity Rate in their individual compensation schedule and the CATEGORY AND LEVEL COMPENSATION RATE SCHEDULE.

Attendance records support payroll review. Report legitimate work that attendance tracking misses through a correction request; missing proof does not automatically forfeit earned wages.

Types of Meetings

Admin Update and Admin Town Hall Meetings

Purpose: To provide comprehensive updates to all staff on organizational changes, initiatives, and announcements.

Frequency: As assigned.

Attendance: Mandatory for all employees. In-town staff must attend in person when applicable; out-of-town staff may attend virtually.

Compensation: Record actual meeting time as Support Activity under the policy above.

Evaluation Meetings

Purpose: To review performance, discuss strengths and areas for improvement, and set professional goals.

Format: As assigned.

Attendance: Mandatory for designated staff.

Compensation: Record actual meeting time as Support Activity under the policy above.

Leadership Circle Meetings

Purpose: To discuss strategic initiatives, leadership development, and organizational alignment.

Frequency: Monthly.

Format: Virtual.

Attendance: Mandatory for leadership team members and designated staff in leadership roles.

Compensation: Record actual meeting time as Support Activity under the policy above.

Supervisor Meetings

Purpose: To support oversight, communication, and alignment related to clinical, operational, and administrative responsibilities.

Frequency: Monthly.

Format: As assigned.

Attendance: Mandatory for supervisors and designated supervisory staff.

Compensation: Record actual operational meeting time as Support Activity. Assigned clinical supervision follows the separately agreed supervision rates in Actual time, support activities and corrections.

SUPERVISION PROCEDURES

Supervision at Next Level Up is structured to ensure compliance, professional growth, and client safety. All procedures outlined below apply across Pre-Licensed Providers, Students, and Unlicensed Providers, unless otherwise noted.

Session Logging and Codes:

Record individual/triadic supervision in the app’s supervision session, identifying the supervisor, supervisee, actual attendance and duration.

Record group supervision in the app’s group supervision session, identifying the supervisor, attendees and actual duration.

Documentation and Summaries:

Session summaries: Keep an accurate, reviewed session summary in the app’s supervision record. Authorized summary tools may assist; the supervisor and supervisee remain responsible for accuracy. A full transcript is not required. Follow App records, forms and timekeeping.

Missing summaries must be completed and may delay verification of supervision documentation or licensure records. Record only verified qualifying hours. Missing documentation does not erase wages earned for compensable work; see Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Attendance and Platform:

Use the app for supervision meetings, attendance, reviewed summaries and time records; follow App records, forms and timekeeping.

Attendance must be punctual, and any absence requires prior notification to both the supervisor and the Support Team.

An unreported supervision absence may be reviewed under Compensation levels: expectations, good standing and review. Protected leave and reasonable accommodations are excluded from adverse consideration; arrange appropriate notice, rescheduling, and clinical coverage.

Voluntary vs. Mandatory Group Supervision:

Mandatory Group Supervision:

Offered bi-weekly.

Required for interns and unlicensed clinicians.

At least one session per month may be mandatory for pre-licensed staff, depending on caseload and supervisor discretion.

Voluntary Group Supervision:

Available to all staff, up to two sessions per month at no cost.

Milestone Transition (Pre-Licensed Only):

The pre-licensed milestone is 60 completed individual/triadic supervision hours plus 40 group supervision opportunities offered. Offered group opportunities are not recorded as hours attended or completed. Once both conditions are met, the individual/triadic entitlement transitions to one hour per month, scheduled as two 30-minute sessions. A supervisor may further reduce frequency based on clinical need, caseload and performance, while maintaining required oversight.

Required supervision and other compensable employee work remain payable under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Benefit tiers, milestone status, missing documentation, or a missing tracking option do not erase pay for work performed. Record actual time and request correction when needed. Supervisor compensation remains 100% of the contracted rate for direct supervision, 150% for actual group hosting time, and 50% for actual review/co-signing of another provider’s notes. These supervisor rates do not automatically set the supervisee’s participation rate.

Group supervision: Continues to be available at no cost and does not count against monthly individual/triadic entitlements.

Optional individual/triadic supervision beyond the applicable benefit entitlement requires advance authorization and available resources. The supplied cost-recovery terms are a warning for the first unauthorized excess session and $50 per hour thereafter, administered by People Operations under the applicable agreement and authorized cost-recovery procedures. Required work remains subject to Actual time, support activities and corrections; a supervision charge does not authorize unpaid work or an automatic deduction from earned wages.

Documentation: Use the app for supervision meetings, attendance, reviewed summaries and time records; follow App records, forms and timekeeping. Keep an accurate, reviewed session summary in the app’s supervision record. Authorized summary tools may assist; the supervisor and supervisee remain responsible for accuracy. A full transcript is not required.

Out of Compliance:

Providers below Tier 1 are considered Out of Compliance:

Below Tier 1 affects the optional tier-funded individual supervision benefit, subject to BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:. It does not remove required oversight or pay for compensable employee work.

Eligible for meetings with the Clinical Practice Assistant (CPA), People Operations, Administrative Staff, or the Support Team for caseload development support.

If Out of Compliance for more than six (6) pay periods per year, the provider may be subject to reassignment or employment reclassification.

Supervision entitlements resume once Tier 1 status is restored.

New-employee benefit grace and recovery rules follow BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:. Benefit status does not waive required clinical oversight or actual-work compensation.

ROLES OF THE SUPERVISOR

Supervisors at Next Level Up provide oversight across three domains: Clinical Development, Billing and Compliance, and Integrated Supervision. Each role has distinct functions to ensure supervisees receive appropriate clinical support, administrative oversight, and compliance guidance.

Clinical Development Supervisor:

Definition:

Focuses on developing supervisees’ clinical skills, professionalism, ethical/legal practice, cultural awareness, and crisis management.

Responsibilities:
  • Conducts individual/triadic supervision sessions (logged under 99415).
  • Guides supervisees in applying evidence-based practices and integrating theoretical approaches.
  • Provides constructive feedback on clinical decision-making and therapeutic interactions.
  • Reviews case conceptualizations, treatment planning, and ethical considerations.
  • Supports professional development and helps supervisees set growth-oriented goals.

Does not oversee billing or note signing — role is limited to clinical development.

Billing and Clinical Compliance Supervisor:

Definition:

Oversees supervisee documentation and compliance practices, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to legal/organizational standards.

Responsibilities:

Record actual time reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes in the app’s supervision and payroll workflow. Compensation is 50% of the supervisor’s individually contracted supervision hourly rate per actual review hour under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Keep the required clinical signatures in the app’s clinical record and do not duplicate compensation.

Reviews supervisee documentation for accuracy and compliance with state, payer, and organizational requirements.

Provides corrective feedback on documentation when needed.

Meets with supervisees occasionally for billing-specific consultation (up to 1 session per quarter, at the supervisor’s discretion).

Coordinates with the Compliance Team to complete formal reviews (Appendix H).

Does not provide clinical development but may flag clinical issues that surface in documentation.

Integrated Clinical and Billing Supervisor:

Definition:

Combines both clinical development and billing/compliance responsibilities into one supervisory role.

Responsibilities:

Provides both individual/triadic supervision (clinical) and admin oversight (note signing, compliance).

Record direct clinical supervision and actual note-review/co-signing time separately under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Direct supervision uses 100% of the individually contracted supervision rate; group hosting uses 150%; reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes uses 50% per actual review hour. Follow the app’s supervision record and approved payroll mapping; a code alone does not establish psychotherapy credits.

Reviews documentation for accuracy while also guiding clinical skills, ethics, and client safety.

Serves as a single point of accountability for supervisees’ professional development and compliance requirements.

General Notes for All Supervisor Roles:

Meeting platform: Use the app for supervision meetings, attendance, reviewed summaries and time records; follow App records, forms and timekeeping.

Session summaries: Keep an accurate, reviewed session summary in the app’s supervision record. Authorized summary tools may assist; the supervisor and supervisee remain responsible for accuracy. A full transcript is not required. Complete missing documentation; handle verification or performance concerns separately from compensation for actual work.

Batch signing: Supervisors are encouraged to batch note review and signing for efficiency. Record actual review time in the app workflow; keep clinical signatures in the app’s clinical record and report work the tracker misses.

Auditing: app activity (log-ins, timestamps, note signing) may be audited periodically. This safeguard protects against errors or misconduct but is not intended as micromanagement.

Milestone adjustment: The pre-licensed milestone is 60 completed individual/triadic supervision hours plus 40 group supervision opportunities offered. Offered group opportunities are not recorded as hours attended or completed. The monthly individual/triadic entitlement and optional excess-session terms are defined in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE SUPERVISOR

Supervisors at Next Level Up play a critical role in supporting the clinical, professional, and administrative development of supervisees. Supervisors are both mentors and gatekeepers of the profession, balancing growth and accountability to ensure safe and effective client care.

Documentation and Note-Signing Requirement:

Record actual time reviewing and co-signing another provider’s notes through the app’s supervision and payroll workflow. Pay is 50% of the individually contracted supervision hourly rate per actual review hour under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Do not include the supervisor’s own notes or add an automatic allowance per supervision hour.

Batch note signing when practical for efficiency and clear records. Retain required signatures in the app’s clinical record and request correction of legitimate work omitted by automatic tracking.

Supervisors should avoid signing personal notes during this time.

Keep an accurate, reviewed session summary in the app’s supervision record. Authorized summary tools may assist; the supervisor and supervisee remain responsible for accuracy. A full transcript is not required. Use the authorized platform and tools described in App records, forms and timekeeping.

Complete missing supervision summaries and address documentation deficiencies through review. Missing documentation does not erase compensation for work actually performed.

Timeliness:

Supervisors are to create a schedule so that they may sign supervisee notes within 72 hours of their initial finalization.

Supervisors must complete all required note signing in the app by 12:00 PM on Tuesday following the end of each workweek.

Delays or failures in documentation may trigger compliance review.

Oversight and Support:

  • Provide clinical oversight, including guidance on treatment planning, ethical issues, crisis intervention, and professional skill development.
  • Encouraging the integration of theoretical knowledge into clinical practice to ensure a comprehensive and well-rounded approach.
  • Maintain a supportive supervisory relationship, offering mentorship and constructive feedback.
  • Monitor supervisee caseloads, ensuring service delivery is ethical, compliant, and within professional scope.
  • Distinguish clearly between Clinical Development Supervision and Billing/Compliance Supervision to prevent role confusion, as necessary.

Capacity and Tiers:

Supervisors must follow the tier-based supervision capacity limits, including the equivalent of 10 supervision hours per week and the communicated 36-credit service scheduling limit. These are workload controls, not limits on recording or paying actual work. Record all compensable supervision, clinical work, review and administrative time under Actual time, support activities and corrections.

For example, 10 supervisees in Tier 1 will net 10 hours per month of individual supervision or 2.5 hours, on average, per week.

Supervisors are responsible for declining supervisees if workload exceeds capacity.

Evaluation and Accountability:

  • Conduct quarterly evaluations using the appropriate rubrics (Appendix G for clinical development, Appendix H for billing/compliance).
  • Address deficiencies with corrective action plans, additional supervision (if required), or caseload adjustments.
  • Retain discretion to suspend or limit supervisees who pose clinical, ethical, or compliance concerns.

Cost Recovery:

Optional individual/triadic supervision beyond the applicable benefit entitlement requires advance authorization and available resources. The supplied cost-recovery terms are a warning for the first unauthorized excess session and $50 per hour thereafter, administered by People Operations under the applicable agreement and authorized cost-recovery procedures. Required work remains subject to Actual time, support activities and corrections; a supervision charge does not authorize unpaid work or an automatic deduction from earned wages.

Scheduled group supervision and Clinical Practice Assistant meetings are provided at no cost and do not consume the individual/triadic entitlement. The scheduled offerings and voluntary participation allowance follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES.

Auditing and Compliance:

Supervisors’ app activity (log-ins, timestamps, note signing, summaries) may be reviewed periodically for compliance.

Auditing is a safeguard against fraud or misconduct.

Supervisors found to be noncompliant with logging, summaries, or capacity rules may be subject to review and corrective action.

Skill Development:

Supervisors must address the following areas during supervision:

  • Clinical skills development.
  • Professional behaviors.
  • Ethical and legal issues.
  • Cultural considerations.
  • Evidence-based practices.

Supervisee Caseload Access:

All clinical supervisors must have access to the entire caseload and case files of their supervisees, regardless of their supervisory role. Supervisors are expected to periodically review and reference the care being provided to ensure ongoing quality and compliance.

Compliance Oversight:

Billing and Clinical Compliance Supervisors are responsible for the ongoing supervision of clinical notes, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards.

Supervision includes both clinical oversight and adherence to documentation requirements.

Supervisee Capacity:

Supervisors may oversee the equivalent of a maximum of 10 full-time supervisees (or the equivalent for part-time; see Tier information above) for clinical supervision and up to 20 supervisees (or the equivalent for part-time; see Tier information above) for billing and compliance supervision. For combined roles, there will be a maximum of 10 full-time supervisees.

Licensure Requirements for Supervisors:

LPC Supervisors must meet all criteria outlined in 4 CCR 737-1.

LAC, LCSW, LMFT, PsyD/PhD Supervisors must have advanced training and experience in supervising unlicensed clinicians.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE SUPERVISEE

Supervisees at Next Level Up are expected to actively and professionally engage in supervision, recognizing it as both a benefit and a responsibility. The following expectations apply to all supervisees:

Self-Assessment:

Supervisees are expected to regularly self-assess and discuss their clinical competencies, including knowledge, skills, and professional attitudes.

Session Participation and Documentation:

Attendance: Supervisees must attend supervision sessions as scheduled. Absences must be communicated in advance to the supervisor and Support Team, as necessary.

Platform: Use the app for supervision meetings, attendance, reviewed summaries and time records; follow App records, forms and timekeeping.

App supervision records:

Use the corresponding supervision session in the app. Record the actual participants, supervision type, attendance and duration. Payroll applies the approved mapping for each person’s role.

Use the corresponding supervision session in the app. Record the actual participants, supervision type, attendance and duration. Payroll applies the approved mapping for each person’s role.

Summaries: Keep an accurate, reviewed session summary in the app’s supervision record. Authorized summary tools may assist; the supervisor and supervisee remain responsible for accuracy. A full transcript is not required. Missing summaries must be completed for supervision verification; they do not erase pay for actual compensable work.

Professional Conduct:

  • Ethical Standards: Uphold the highest professional and ethical standards in all clinical activities and supervisory interactions.
  • Preparation: Arrive prepared with client cases, documentation, and questions for discussion.
  • Cultural Competence: Incorporate diversity, equity, and cultural considerations into case conceptualizations.
  • Self-Reflection: Remain open to feedback and willing to discuss personal factors that may influence clinical work.

Benefit Tier Alignment:

Supervisees are entitled to supervision based on their Benefit Tier status.

The pre-licensed milestone is 60 completed individual/triadic supervision hours plus 40 group supervision opportunities offered. Offered group opportunities are not recorded as hours attended or completed. Apply the monthly individual/triadic entitlement and any optional excess-session terms in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES.

Scheduled group supervision is provided at no cost and does not consume the individual/triadic entitlement. Voluntary offerings follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES.

Cost Recovery for Excess Supervision:

Optional sessions beyond the benefit entitlement require advance authorization and follow the cost-recovery terms in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES:

  • Receive a warning for the first occurrence.
  • Be subject to out-of-pocket cost recovery at $50 per hour for subsequent occurrences.

Supervisors do not bill supervisees. Cost recovery is managed by the organization.

People Operations administers any authorized cost recovery under the applicable agreement and PAYDAYS, DEDUCTIONS, AND GARNISHMENTS. A charge is not an automatic payroll deduction. Required work remains subject to Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Out of Compliance:

Supervisees who fall below Tier 1 are considered Out of Compliance.

Below Tier 1 affects the optional tier-funded individual supervision benefit, subject to BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:. Caseload-development support remains available through the Clinical Practice Assistant, People Operations, administrative staff or Support Team. Required oversight and compensation for actual work remain applicable.

Optional additional supervision may be requested under the excess-session terms in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES.

Supervision entitlements resume once Tier 1 status is restored.

New-employee benefit grace follows BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:. Required oversight and compensation for actual work remain applicable during and after the grace period.

Independent Tracking and Responsibility:

Supervisees are responsible for maintaining and reviewing their supervision and clinical hours in the app for licensure or academic purposes. Required university or licensing-board verification does not replace the app record.

Supervisors are not responsible for tracking supervisee hours, though they may review and verify documentation when necessary.

Supervisees must ensure their hours are accurate, honest, and reflective of actual time worked.

Emergency Consultation:

Consulting with supervisors in emergency situations to ensure client safety and appropriate intervention.

LEGAL AND ETHICAL COMPLIANCE

Supervisors and supervisees at Next Level Up are expected to uphold the highest professional, ethical, and legal standards in all supervision activities. This section outlines the requirements and responsibilities that govern compliance.

Licensure Requirements for Supervisors:

Eligibility: Only licensed professionals who meet state requirements may serve as supervisors.

Credentials:
  • LPC Supervisors must meet all requirements outlined in 4 CCR 737-1.
  • LAC, LCSW, LMFT, PsyD/PhD Supervisors must have advanced training and experience in supervising unlicensed clinicians.
  • Supervisors must maintain active licensure in good standing throughout their supervisory role.

Ethical Standards:

  • All supervisors and supervisees are expected to follow the ethical guidelines established by their respective licensing boards (e.g., ACA, NASW, APA, AAMFT, NAADAC).
  • Supervisors serve as gatekeepers of the profession, with both the right and responsibility to monitor, pause, or suspend supervisees if ethical or clinical concerns arise.
  • Supervisees must practice within their scope of competence and immediately consult with their supervisor in cases involving client risk or complex clinical issues.

Capacity and Tier Compliance:

Supervision must be conducted within the tier-based capacity system (Tier 1: up to 40 supervisees, Tier 2: up to 20 supervisees, Tier 3: up to 10 supervisees).

Balance assignments within the communicated service and supervision scheduling limits, including the 36-credit service scheduling control. Record all actual compensable time; credits and scheduling limits do not replace work-time records or cap earned pay. See Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Supervisors may not accept supervisees beyond their tier allocation or personal capacity.

Documentation and Transparency:

All supervision sessions must be documented in the app according to organizational policy.

Supervisors and supervisees are both responsible for ensuring that summaries are completed for each session.

Supervisory notes and evaluations are organizational records and may be subject to internal review, compliance audits, or state board requests.

Auditing and Oversight:

Supervisors’ and supervisees’ app activity (log-ins, timestamps, session documentation, and note signing) may be audited periodically to ensure honesty, compliance, and accountability.

Auditing is intended as a safeguard against errors or misconduct and is not meant to serve as micromanagement of staff.

Supervisors and supervisees found falsifying documentation, misrepresenting hours, or otherwise acting in violation of compliance standards will be subject to corrective action, up to and including termination or report to the appropriate licensing body.

Organizational Safeguards:

Next Level Up reserves the right to reassign, limit, or suspend supervisory relationships if compliance, capacity, or ethical standards are not met.

Below Tier 1 affects the optional tier-funded individual supervision benefit, subject to BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:. Support through the Clinical Practice Assistant, People Operations or administrative staff remains available. Required oversight and pay for compensable work are not removed by benefit status.

A supervisee may request optional additional supervision under the authorized excess-session terms in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES. Supervisor-mandated oversight is assigned work; record and compensate actual employee work under Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Corrective Action:

Action Plans: Developed when deficiencies are identified (e.g., unsafe practice, repeated documentation issues). Plans must include clear corrective steps and a follow-up schedule.

Increased oversight: Supervisors may increase required supervision when needed to address clinical or compliance concerns. Required employee work remains compensable; the optional excess-benefit cost-recovery process does not authorize unpaid work or an automatic deduction from earned wages.

Caseload Adjustment: Supervisors may recommend reduction of caseload if supervisees cannot demonstrate safe or compliant practice.

Transparency and Access:

Evaluation Notes: Complete evaluations and rubrics in the app’s Evaluations workflow; keep employee and intern evaluation records separate from client clinical records.

Supervisee Access: Supervisees may request copies of their evaluations and rubrics at any time.

Shared Responsibility: Both supervisor and supervisee must acknowledge and address evaluation outcomes.

SECTION E: Non-Clinical Staff

This section applies to employees and contractors whose roles are administrative, operational, managerial, technical, or support-based and who do not provide clinical or therapeutic services. This includes, but is not limited to administrative staff, operations personnel, coordinators, billing and support staff, outreach staff, and management roles that do not involve clinical service delivery.

Non-Clinical Staff play a vital role in supporting the Practice’s mission by ensuring organizational stability, compliance, coordination, and effective service delivery infrastructure. These roles do not carry clinical authority.

Role Definition and Purpose

Non-Clinical Staff support the Practice through operational and administrative duties such as coordination, communication, billing, scheduling, technology and program support. These duties support client access and continuity of care but do not involve diagnosis, treatment or clinical decision-making. Required meetings, onboarding, training and assigned internal work follow 14. Support Activity and Actual time, support activities and corrections. Use the applicable salary agreement or individual duty rate; an administrative job title does not automatically classify all work as Indirect Service.

Non-Clinical Staff must maintain clear boundaries between operational support and clinical care at all times.

Scope of Responsibilities

When authorized by role and assignment, Non-Clinical Staff may:

  • Perform administrative, operational, scheduling, billing, or coordination tasks
  • Support program logistics, onboarding, data entry, record management, or reporting
  • Communicate with families or partners regarding scheduling, logistics, or non-clinical matters
  • Support staff through coordination, information sharing, and systems management
  • Participate in organizational meetings, trainings, and professional development as required

Non-Clinical Staff must operate strictly within the scope of their assigned duties.

Prohibited Activities and Clinical Boundaries

Non-Clinical Staff may not:

  • Provide clinical services, counseling, or therapeutic interventions
  • Diagnose mental health conditions or make clinical recommendations
  • Interpret clinical information for clients or families
  • Provide guidance that could be construed as clinical advice
  • Represent themselves as clinicians or clinical authorities
  • Engage in documentation intended to serve as clinical records

Any situation involving clinical questions, treatment decisions, or client risk must be escalated to an appropriate clinical provider or supervisor.

Confidentiality and Information Access

Non-Clinical Staff may access client or employee information only as necessary to perform assigned duties and must adhere to all confidentiality, privacy, and HIPAA requirements.

  • Access to clinical records is role-limited and purpose-specific
  • Information obtained through administrative access may not be shared outside authorized channels
  • Confidentiality obligations continue following separation from employment

Improper access, use, or disclosure of information may result in corrective action.

Center-Based and Client-Adjacent Conduct

When Non-Clinical Staff are present in NLU service or client-adjacent environments, they must:

  • Adhere to NLU site professionalism, safety, and conduct standards
  • Maintain appropriate boundaries with students, families, and NLU personnel
  • Avoid involvement in client-specific discussions beyond logistical coordination
  • Refer all clinical questions or concerns to designated clinical staff

Presence in an NLU service or program setting does not authorize clinical engagement.

Communication and Representation

Non-Clinical Staff must represent the Practice accurately and professionally in all communications.

  • Communication with clients or families should remain logistical and informational
  • Clinical questions must be redirected to authorized providers
  • Staff must avoid language that implies clinical judgment, diagnosis, or treatment

All external communications must align with Practice policies and role authorization. Use the app records and secure communication procedures in App records, forms and timekeeping.

Supervision, Accountability, and Escalation

Non-Clinical Staff are accountable to their designated supervisor or manager.

  • Concerns related to safety, ethics, compliance, or boundary issues must be escalated promptly
  • Non-Clinical Staff must seek guidance when uncertain about role boundaries
  • Failure to maintain boundaries or comply with Practice policies may result in corrective action

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Workplace Policies and Standards
  • Confidentiality and Privacy
  • Performance and Expectations

Where conflicts arise, non-clinical role limitations prevail.

Section E Summary

Non-Clinical Staff support the Practice through essential administrative and operational functions while maintaining clear boundaries from clinical service delivery. This section establishes expectations that protect clients, staff, and the organization by preventing role confusion and ensuring appropriate escalation of clinical matters.

SECTION D: Licensed Providers and Clinical Supervisors (Tier 3)

This section applies to employees holding an active, unrestricted clinical license recognized by the Practice, including Licensed Professional Counselors (LPC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFT), Licensed Clinical Social Workers (LCSW), and other licensed clinicians authorized by Next Level Up to provide independent clinical services.

Licensed Providers may also hold Clinical Supervisor designations when approved by the Practice. Tier 3 providers are entrusted with the highest level of clinical authority, accountability, and professional responsibility within the organization.

Role Definition and Professional Authority

Licensed Providers are authorized to practice independently within the scope of their license and Practice approval. This includes full responsibility for clinical decision-making, treatment planning, risk assessment, and therapeutic intervention.

Licensed Providers serve as the clinical backbone of the Practice, supporting client care, supervising less-credentialed staff when designated, and upholding ethical, legal, and professional standards across programs and settings.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Clinical Activities

When credentialed and authorized by the Practice, Licensed Providers may:

  • Provide authorized individual, family and collateral psychotherapy. Client group psychotherapy requires existing written authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Conduct clinical assessments, establish diagnoses, and determine medical necessity
  • Develop, modify, and terminate treatment plans independently
  • Select and implement evidence-based clinical interventions within licensure scope
  • Provide crisis assessment, intervention, and stabilization
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams and external providers
  • Deliver services in approved NLU office and telehealth settings
  • Participate in program development, consultation, and leadership activities

Licensed Providers are responsible for ensuring all services align with licensure requirements, payer rules, and Practice standards.

Clinical Judgment, Risk, and Crisis Authority

Licensed Providers retain primary authority and responsibility for:

  • Risk assessment and safety planning
  • Determination of clinical urgency and escalation
  • Crisis intervention and post-crisis follow-up
  • Mandatory reporting decisions
  • Ethical decision-making and professional boundaries

When supervising others, Licensed Providers must actively monitor risk, intervene as needed, and ensure appropriate documentation and follow-up.

Supervision Responsibilities and Oversight Authority

Licensed Providers approved as Clinical Supervisors hold formal oversight responsibility for supervisees.

Supervisory responsibilities may include:

  • Clinical oversight and guidance
  • Review and co-signing of documentation
  • Ensuring supervisee compliance with scope, ethics, and payer rules
  • Providing feedback, education, and corrective guidance
  • Escalating concerns related to safety, performance, or compliance

Supervisors retain shared accountability for services provided under their supervision. Failure to supervise appropriately may result in corrective action or removal of supervisory designation.

The structure and mechanics of supervision follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES. Direct supervision is paid at 100% of the individually contracted supervision hourly rate, group hosting at 150%, and actual review/co-signing of another provider’s notes at 50%, under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Clinical oversight duties and pay for actual work remain separate from payer reimbursement.

Documentation and Accountability

Licensed Providers are responsible for ensuring that documentation:

  • Accurately reflects services provided
  • Supports diagnosis, medical necessity, and treatment rationale
  • Meets payer, regulatory, and Practice standards
  • Is completed timely and accurately

When supervising others, Licensed Providers are responsible for reviewing documentation and addressing deficiencies. Repeated documentation issues may trigger audits or corrective action.

Billing and Compliance Responsibility

Licensed Providers may bill services in accordance with credentialing status, payer rules, and Practice authorization.

Licensed Providers must:

  • Ensure services billed are appropriate, authorized, and compliant
  • Avoid misrepresentation of services or credentials
  • Oversee billing activity for supervised staff when applicable

Billing execution and coding rules follow Service-code compensation and authorizations and applicable billing policies. Client group services require written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization. Obtain approval before advertising, enrolling or scheduling; a role, credential or saved code mapping does not authorize group delivery.

Ethical Leadership and Professional Conduct

Licensed Providers are expected to model ethical conduct, professionalism, and clinical integrity across all settings.

This includes:

  • Adherence to licensure board ethics and legal requirements
  • Maintenance of professional boundaries
  • Appropriate use of authority and influence
  • Respectful collaboration with staff, clients, and partners
  • Avoidance of role confusion or scope drift

Licensed Providers are expected to uphold Practice values and serve as professional leaders within the organization.

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Supervision and Training
  • Legal and Ethical Compliance
  • Career Pathways and Compensation
  • Service-code compensation and authorizations
  • Program-Specific Sections

Where conflicts arise, licensure requirements, payer rules, and supervisory responsibility prevail.

Section D Summary

Licensed Providers and Clinical Supervisors hold the highest level of clinical authority and accountability within the Practice. This section establishes independent practice authority while clearly defining supervisory responsibility, ethical leadership expectations, and compliance obligations to protect clients, staff, and the organization.

SUPERVISION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

Mentorship:

Each student is paired with a mentor, titled “Clinical Practice Assistant,” for, at minimum, biweekly sessions and initial orientation. Mentors provide guidance across various aspects of the program, including additional educational activities.

Supervision:

Regular supervision sessions, at least once weekly, are conducted with an assigned supervisor. These sessions are critical for feedback, performance evaluation, and aligning with educational objectives. This student-program requirement is separate from the pre-licensed 60/40 benefit transition. Use SUPERVISION PROCEDURES for authorized platforms, reviewed summaries and documentation; separately employed students’ compensable work follows Actual time, support activities and corrections.

STUDENT CLASSIFICATION

Practicum students and interns participate as trainees under the applicable training or affiliation agreement. Employee status requires a separate written employment agreement, consistent with WORKFORCE CLASSIFICATIONS and SECTION B: Intern Mental Health Providers. A training placement does not automatically make a student an employee or a 1099 contractor. Where a student also holds an employee role, the individual employment agreement and applicable employee compensation, timekeeping, leave and benefit policies govern that work. Training purpose does not remove protections applicable to an employee.

PROGRAM STRUCTURE

Phases of Engagement

Practicum Phase:

For students starting their practical training, this phase focuses on foundational learning and skill development within a structured, supervised environment.

Internship Phase:

Designed for students who have either completed the practicum phase or possess equivalent experience, this phase offers an opportunity for deeper immersion into practical work, allowing students to refine their skills and knowledge in a real-world setting.

Placement Status

Students are engaged as part of our team, either as practicum students or interns, for a specific period. The program begins effectively on a predetermined Commencement Date, with the possibility of transitioning between phases based on successful completion and mutual agreement. Participation is a training placement; any separate employee engagement must be documented under STUDENT CLASSIFICATION.

Ending the Placement

Either the student or the Practice may end the training agreement under its terms. A separate employee engagement is governed by its written employment agreement and the applicable employee policies; placement participation alone does not create employee status.

Location and Scope

Student placements occur at approved NLU centers and through approved virtual services under the training plan and required supervision. Assignments distinguish academic tutoring, group skills and clinical counseling.

Focus on Education and Training:

Regardless of the phase, the primary purpose of the program is educational. Whether students are engaged in billable services or other professional activities, the emphasis remains on learning, skill development, and professional growth.

EXPECTATIONS OF STUDENT

Duties and Professional Conduct:

Students are required to perform duties under Practice supervision, focusing on educational and professional development objectives. This includes adhering to ethical standards and professional conduct as required by regulatory and accrediting authorities.

Participation in Services:

Students' involvement in billable services is subject to Practice evaluation, ensuring alignment with educational goals. Written role, payer and program authorization remain required under Service-code compensation and authorizations. Client group services require written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization. Obtain approval before advertising, enrolling or scheduling; a role, credential or saved code mapping does not authorize group delivery.

Documentation and Reporting:

Complete session notes SHOULD be completed and submitted within 24 hours of each session.

Completed session notes MUST be submitted by Sunday night at 11:59pm of the week for which the session occurred.

Notes completed outside of this timeframe are considered Late and Deficient. Documentation deficiencies may affect training review and must be corrected. For students separately engaged as employees, a late note does not erase pay for compensable work; follow Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Feedback and Compliance:

Students are expected to discuss concerns with their supervisor and comply with all Practice regulations and instructions, including those governing work conditions and legal ordinances.

Specific Duties:

These include, but are not limited to, observing and conducting counseling sessions, participating in intake assessments, completing administrative tasks, maintaining client confidentiality, and engaging in outreach activities. Duties must remain within the approved training plan and role scope. Client group work requires the written authorization in Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization.
