SECTION A: Clinical Support Providers (Tier 1)

Applicability and Role Categories

This section applies to employees functioning in Tier 1 Clinical Support roles, which include distinct subcategories with different authorization limits, specifically:

  • Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers (e.g., Bachelor’s-Level Mental Health Counselors)
  • Non-Degree Clinical Support Providers, including:
  • Qualified Behavioral Health Assistants (QBHA)
  • Peer Support Professionals

While all Tier 1 roles operate under supervision and without independent clinical authority, authorization to provide, document, or bill specific services varies by subcategory and is governed by payer rules, program approval, and Practice authorization.

Tier 1 classification alone does not confer uniform service or billing authority.

Role Definition and Purpose

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers expand access to mental health–related services through structured support, skill development, facilitation, engagement, and reinforcement of treatment goals. These roles are designed to complement, not replace, clinical services delivered by Master’s-level or licensed providers.

Tier 1 providers function within Practice-approved programs (including office-based, telehealth, and approved skill development settings) and support client progress through goal-oriented, skill-based interventions aligned with assigned scope and supervision.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Activities

Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers

When explicitly authorized by the Practice and permitted by payer and program rules, Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers may:

  • Deliver structured individual support services, including H0004 (Behavioral Health Counseling and Therapy) when all authorization, documentation, and supervision requirements are met
  • Facilitate or co-facilitate skill-based, psychoeducational or prevention-focused client groups only within written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Reinforce treatment goals, coping strategies, and behavioral skills established by supervising clinicians
  • Support emotional regulation, social skills, communication, frustration tolerance, and functional improvement
  • Observe, track, and report client progress and engagement
  • Participate in office-based or telehealth services consistent with consent and program scope

Provision of H0004 by Bachelor’s-Level providers does not constitute independent psychotherapy authority and must occur strictly within the approved treatment/service plan and supervision structure.

QBHA and Peer Support Professionals

Qualified Behavioral Health Assistants (QBHA) and Peer Support Professionals may not provide or bill H0004 or any other counseling/therapy codes.

When authorized, these roles may:

  • Deliver non-therapy, skill-based, rehabilitative, outreach, or support services permitted under applicable codes and programs
  • Facilitate or assist with structured client groups only when the program, role and service are authorized under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Support engagement, skill practice, and functional goal reinforcement
  • Provide observation-based feedback to supervising clinicians
  • Participate in approved NLU programming consistent with training and authorization

All services provided by QBHAs and Peer Support Professionals must remain non-clinical in nature and may not be represented as counseling or therapy.

Prohibited Activities and Clinical Limitations (All Tier 1 Roles)

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers may not:

  • Independently diagnose mental health conditions
  • Independently develop, modify, or terminate treatment plans without approval of a licensed and approved clinical supervisor.
  • Provide psychotherapy services reserved for Master’s-level or licensed clinicians
  • Assume service or billing authority based on job title or Tier placement alone
  • Operate outside assigned program scope or supervision
  • Use clinical terminology or representations that exceed authorized scope

Supervision Expectations

All Tier 1 providers are supervised at all times.

  • Supervision requirements apply regardless of experience or tenure
  • Supervision does not confer independent clinical authority
  • Providers must escalate scope questions, safety concerns, or uncertainty through supervisory channels
  • Supervision structure, frequency, and documentation follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES and the applicable role and training requirements. Required compensable employee work follows Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Documentation Responsibilities

Tier 1 providers are responsible for completing accurate, timely documentation consistent with:

  • Authorized service descriptions
  • Program requirements
  • Coding and billing rules
  • Scope limitations tied to their specific role category

Documentation must remain within the role’s scope and be accurate, timely and complete. Documentation deficiencies may require correction or corrective action. A late note or other documentation concern does not erase earned wages; follow Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Billing and Service Authorization

  • Tier 1 providers may bill services only when explicitly authorized
  • Authorization to bill does not imply clinical independence
  • Providers are responsible for confirming authorization prior to service delivery
  • Billing rules, code eligibility and compensation mappings follow Service-code compensation and authorizations and the individual compensation schedule. Client group services require written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization. Obtain approval before advertising, enrolling or scheduling; a role, credential or saved code mapping does not authorize group delivery.

Do not provide or bill services outside written authorization, scope or payer requirements. Address unauthorized activity through compliance review and correction. Missing preapproval or a denied claim does not erase wages earned for work actually performed; see Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Center-Based and Group Setting Standards

When operating in center-based or group settings, Tier 1 providers must:

  • Adhere to NLU site professionalism, safety, and confidentiality requirements
  • Maintain appropriate professional boundaries
  • Follow escalation and crisis protocols
  • Represent the Practice consistently and professionally

Center-based placement does not expand scope of practice or billing authority.

  • Workplace Policies and Standards
  • Supervision and Training
  • Role Descriptions and Typical Duties
  • Service-code compensation and authorizations
  • Program-Specific Sections (e.g., Therapy + Tutoring program)

Section A Summary

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers contribute meaningful, structured services through supervised, skill-based, and program-aligned interventions. While Bachelor’s-Level providers may be authorized to deliver certain counseling services such as H0004, QBHAs and Peer Support Professionals are limited to non-therapy support roles. This section establishes clear internal distinctions to protect clients, staff, and the Practice while ensuring compliant, defensible service delivery.

SECTION B: Intern Mental Health Providers

This section applies to individuals participating in Next Level Up’s Student Training Program as practicum students, interns, or trainees enrolled in an approved academic program. Intern Mental Health Providers function in a training capacity and do not hold independent clinical authority or employee status unless expressly stated in a written agreement.

Interns provide services solely for educational and training purposes under close supervision and within strict scope-of-practice limitations defined by the Practice, the academic institution, and applicable law.

Role Definition and Educational Purpose

The Intern Mental Health Provider role exists to support the student’s academic and professional development through supervised, hands-on clinical experience. Internship placements are designed to meet educational requirements while maintaining client safety, ethical practice, and compliance with regulatory and payer standards.

Intern participation does not guarantee employment, future role placement, or advancement within the Practice.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Activities

When authorized by the Practice and academic institution, Intern Mental Health Providers may:

  • Observe, assist, co-facilitate, and conduct counseling sessions under supervision
  • Participate in intake processes and assist with gathering clinical information
  • Support the development and implementation of treatment or service plans in collaboration with supervising clinicians
  • Apply evidence-informed, developmentally appropriate interventions consistent with training level
  • Facilitate or support client group sessions only within the approved training and supervision plan and the written authorization required by Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Provide services in approved NLU office and telehealth settings as assigned

All services must be approved in advance, supervised, and aligned with the intern’s training level and educational objectives.

Prohibited Activities and Clinical Limitations

Intern Mental Health Providers may not:

  • Practice independently or without supervision
  • Independently develop, modify, or terminate treatment plans or diagnose mental disorders without the approval of a Licensed Clinical Supervisor.
  • Represent themselves as licensed or independently credentialed providers
  • Provide services outside approved programs, supervision, or training agreements
  • Bill services independently or assume billing authority

Interns must not exceed the scope authorized by the Practice or academic institution, regardless of prior experience.

Supervision Requirements and Authority

Intern Mental Health Providers are subject to direct clinical supervision at all times.

  • Supervisors are designated by the Practice
  • Supervisors retain full clinical responsibility for services provided by interns
  • Supervisors must approve services, documentation, and clinical decisions
  • Interns must participate in individual supervision, group supervision, case reviews, and training as required

Supervision structure, documentation and tracking follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES and SUPERVISION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. Student placements retain their program-specific supervision requirements; the pre-licensed 60/40 benefit milestone does not automatically reduce student supervision.

Documentation Responsibilities

Interns are responsible for completing documentation accurately and timely, consistent with training level and Practice standards.

Documentation:

  • Must be reviewed and co-signed by the designated supervisor
  • Must remain within intern scope and training expectations
  • Must adhere to documentation timelines and correction procedures

Incomplete, late, or inaccurate documentation may impact training status or continuation in the program.

Billing and Compensation

Intern Mental Health Providers do not bill independently.

  • Any billing of intern-provided services occurs under the supervising clinician’s authority
  • Billing eligibility and codes require written Practice and payer authorization, supervision and an applicable training agreement. Employment status and any compensation follow STUDENT CLASSIFICATION and the individual written agreement.
  • Training participation alone does not authorize billing or determine employee status. For students separately engaged as employees, compensable work remains payable under Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Unauthorized billing activity is prohibited.

Professional Conduct and Center-Based Expectations

Interns are expected to maintain professional conduct consistent with Practice policies, academic training standards, and NLU site requirements.

Interns must:

  • Adhere to confidentiality and HIPAA requirements
  • Maintain appropriate boundaries with clients, families, and NLU team members
  • Follow escalation and safety protocols
  • Represent the Practice professionally in all settings

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Student Training Program
  • Supervision and Training
  • Workplace Policies and Standards
  • Role Descriptions and Typical Duties (when applicable)
  • Program-Specific Sections

Where conflicts arise, educational purpose and supervision authority prevail.

Section B Summary

Intern Mental Health Providers participate in structured, supervised training experiences that prioritize learning, ethical practice, and client safety. This section defines the boundaries and expectations of intern roles to prevent scope drift, ensure compliance, and support high-quality training outcomes.

SECTION C: Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers (Tier 2)

This section applies to employees who hold a Master’s degree in a mental health–related field and are functioning in roles that require advanced clinical knowledge but do not confer independent licensure authority. This includes pre-licensed clinicians actively pursuing licensure and unlicensed Master’s-level providers practicing in roles where licensure is not required or not applicable.

Tier 2 providers deliver clinical and therapeutic services under defined supervision requirements and within Practice-approved scope. Authorization to provide or bill services is determined by credentialing status, supervision, payer requirements, and program approval—not solely by degree attainment or licensure intent.

Role Definition and Professional Standing

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers occupy an intermediate role between training positions and fully licensed clinical practice. These providers are qualified to deliver therapeutic services consistent with their education and training but remain subject to ongoing oversight, supervision, and Practice authorization.

Licensure pursuit may be required, optional, or not applicable depending on role designation, program assignment, and funding source. Regardless of licensure intent, Tier 2 providers do not practice independently.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Clinical Activities

When authorized by the Practice, Tier 2 providers may:

  • Provide authorized individual and family-based therapeutic services aligned with approved treatment or service plans. Client group delivery also requires the written authorization in Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Conduct clinical assessments and contribute to diagnostic impressions under supervision
  • Develop, implement, and update treatment plans subject to supervisory review
  • Utilize evidence-based and developmentally appropriate clinical interventions consistent with training and supervision
  • Collaborate with families and interdisciplinary teams as permitted by consent
  • Provide services in approved NLU office and telehealth settings as assigned

Tier 2 providers may exercise clinical judgment within their authorized scope, subject to supervision and escalation requirements.

Clinical Authority Limits and Prohibited Activities

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers may not:

  • Practice independently or without required supervision
  • Represent themselves as fully licensed clinicians
  • Provide services outside approved credentialing, payer, or program authorization
  • Ignore or override supervisory direction
  • Assume authority for high-risk clinical decisions without consultation

Independent practice authority is not granted until full licensure and Practice approval are obtained.

Supervision Requirements and Milestones

Tier 2 providers are subject to structured clinical supervision.

  • Supervision frequency, format, and documentation are determined by licensure status, payer rules, and Practice policy
  • Supervisors retain oversight authority and may review, co-sign, or redirect clinical work
  • Providers must escalate safety concerns, ethical dilemmas, scope questions, or complex cases

For pre-licensed providers, supervision may also count toward licensure requirements when conducted by an approved supervisor. Milestone transitions (e.g., increased autonomy, expanded caseloads) are not automatic and require documented approval. For the pre-licensed benefit transition, use the confirmed 60 completed individual/triadic hours plus 40 group opportunities offered in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES. Offered opportunities are not completed licensure hours, and this milestone does not create independent practice authority.

Documentation Responsibilities

Tier 2 providers are responsible for timely, accurate, and clinically appropriate documentation.

Documentation must:

  • Support medical necessity and clinical rationale
  • Accurately reflect services provided and interventions used
  • Align with treatment plans and service authorization
  • Comply with payer, regulatory, and Practice standards

Documentation may be subject to supervisory review, audit, and correction.

Billing and Service Authorization

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers may bill services only when authorized by the Practice and permitted by payer and program rules.

  • Billing eligibility depends on credentialing, supervision, and payer requirements
  • Providers must confirm authorization prior to service delivery
  • Billing execution, code authorization and compensation follow Service-code compensation and authorizations, the individual employment agreement and Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Unauthorized or non-compliant billing may result in corrective action.

Center-Based and Interdisciplinary Practice

When practicing in center-based or interdisciplinary environments, Tier 2 providers must:

  • Maintain professional boundaries and role clarity
  • Coordinate appropriately with NLU personnel while adhering to confidentiality requirements
  • Follow escalation, safety, and crisis protocols
  • Represent the Practice professionally and within scope

Program placement does not expand or alter clinical authority.

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Supervision and Training
  • Career Pathways and Compensation
  • Service-code compensation and authorizations
  • Role Descriptions and Typical Duties
  • Program-Specific Sections

Where conflicts arise, supervision requirements and payer authorization prevail.

Section C Summary

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers deliver advanced clinical services under supervision while progressing toward greater professional responsibility. This section establishes clear authority limits, supervision expectations, and billing boundaries to ensure ethical practice, regulatory compliance, and client safety.

SECTION D: Licensed Providers and Clinical Supervisors (Tier 3)

This section applies to employees holding an active, unrestricted clinical license recognized by the Practice, including Licensed Professional Counselors (LPC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFT), Licensed Clinical Social Workers (LCSW), and other licensed clinicians authorized by Next Level Up to provide independent clinical services.

Licensed Providers may also hold Clinical Supervisor designations when approved by the Practice. Tier 3 providers are entrusted with the highest level of clinical authority, accountability, and professional responsibility within the organization.

Role Definition and Professional Authority

Licensed Providers are authorized to practice independently within the scope of their license and Practice approval. This includes full responsibility for clinical decision-making, treatment planning, risk assessment, and therapeutic intervention.

Licensed Providers serve as the clinical backbone of the Practice, supporting client care, supervising less-credentialed staff when designated, and upholding ethical, legal, and professional standards across programs and settings.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Clinical Activities

When credentialed and authorized by the Practice, Licensed Providers may:

  • Provide authorized individual, family and collateral psychotherapy. Client group psychotherapy requires existing written authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Conduct clinical assessments, establish diagnoses, and determine medical necessity
  • Develop, modify, and terminate treatment plans independently
  • Select and implement evidence-based clinical interventions within licensure scope
  • Provide crisis assessment, intervention, and stabilization
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams and external providers
  • Deliver services in approved NLU office and telehealth settings
  • Participate in program development, consultation, and leadership activities

Licensed Providers are responsible for ensuring all services align with licensure requirements, payer rules, and Practice standards.

Clinical Judgment, Risk, and Crisis Authority

Licensed Providers retain primary authority and responsibility for:

  • Risk assessment and safety planning
  • Determination of clinical urgency and escalation
  • Crisis intervention and post-crisis follow-up
  • Mandatory reporting decisions
  • Ethical decision-making and professional boundaries

When supervising others, Licensed Providers must actively monitor risk, intervene as needed, and ensure appropriate documentation and follow-up.

Supervision Responsibilities and Oversight Authority

Licensed Providers approved as Clinical Supervisors hold formal oversight responsibility for supervisees.

Supervisory responsibilities may include:

  • Clinical oversight and guidance
  • Review and co-signing of documentation
  • Ensuring supervisee compliance with scope, ethics, and payer rules
  • Providing feedback, education, and corrective guidance
  • Escalating concerns related to safety, performance, or compliance

Supervisors retain shared accountability for services provided under their supervision. Failure to supervise appropriately may result in corrective action or removal of supervisory designation.

The structure and mechanics of supervision follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES. Direct supervision is paid at 100% of the individually contracted supervision hourly rate, group hosting at 150%, and actual review/co-signing of another provider’s notes at 50%, under Actual time, support activities and corrections. Clinical oversight duties and pay for actual work remain separate from payer reimbursement.

Documentation and Accountability

Licensed Providers are responsible for ensuring that documentation:

  • Accurately reflects services provided
  • Supports diagnosis, medical necessity, and treatment rationale
  • Meets payer, regulatory, and Practice standards
  • Is completed timely and accurately

When supervising others, Licensed Providers are responsible for reviewing documentation and addressing deficiencies. Repeated documentation issues may trigger audits or corrective action.

Billing and Compliance Responsibility

Licensed Providers may bill services in accordance with credentialing status, payer rules, and Practice authorization.

Licensed Providers must:

  • Ensure services billed are appropriate, authorized, and compliant
  • Avoid misrepresentation of services or credentials
  • Oversee billing activity for supervised staff when applicable

Billing execution and coding rules follow Service-code compensation and authorizations and applicable billing policies. Client group services require written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization. Obtain approval before advertising, enrolling or scheduling; a role, credential or saved code mapping does not authorize group delivery.

Ethical Leadership and Professional Conduct

Licensed Providers are expected to model ethical conduct, professionalism, and clinical integrity across all settings.

This includes:

  • Adherence to licensure board ethics and legal requirements
  • Maintenance of professional boundaries
  • Appropriate use of authority and influence
  • Respectful collaboration with staff, clients, and partners
  • Avoidance of role confusion or scope drift

Licensed Providers are expected to uphold Practice values and serve as professional leaders within the organization.

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Supervision and Training
  • Legal and Ethical Compliance
  • Career Pathways and Compensation
  • Service-code compensation and authorizations
  • Program-Specific Sections

Where conflicts arise, licensure requirements, payer rules, and supervisory responsibility prevail.

Section D Summary

Licensed Providers and Clinical Supervisors hold the highest level of clinical authority and accountability within the Practice. This section establishes independent practice authority while clearly defining supervisory responsibility, ethical leadership expectations, and compliance obligations to protect clients, staff, and the organization.

updates.subject: Spanish-language intake and handoff
updates.changed_content:
Spanish-language intake and handoff

Record the client’s and parent/guardian’s primary languages separately in the app’s intake record and client profile. When a parent or guardian prefers Spanish, arrange a Spanish-speaking parent intake through the agency’s Spanish intake team.

  1. Request availability: Open Messages by Conversa and choose the Spanish / Español group. Request a parent-intake time without posting identifying clinical information to the group.
  2. Assign the Spanish-speaking provider: Support coordinates the handoff and adds that provider to the individual client’s authorized care team. Group membership alone does not grant access to client records.
  3. Complete the intake: The Spanish-speaking provider conducts the parent intake and completes its documentation in the client record. The primary provider may attend if helpful.
  4. Prepare the care summary: The primary provider uses the Note Aid treatment-summary workflow to prepare a brief, relevant summary, reviews it for accuracy, and saves the reviewed summary in the authorized medical record. The assigned Spanish-speaking provider accesses it there.
  5. Continue coordination: The assigned Spanish-speaking provider handles future parent check-ins and coordination of care, documenting contacts and sharing relevant updates with the primary provider through the client record.
  6. When coverage is unavailable: Ask support to arrange appropriate language assistance. Do not use children as interpreters or treat an unsuccessful English-language contact as a refusal of services.

In your Provider Update, list languages you can use proficiently enough to conduct sessions and select your proficiency. Update support when your availability changes.

updates.subject: Business cards and public profiles
updates.changed_content:
Business cards and public profiles

You can print your own Next Level Up business cards at the office. Preprinted cardstock with the Next Level Up website QR code will be available, so you can print your provider information on the other side.

How to print
  1. Check your profile first. Open your public provider profile from the Provider Update and make sure your name, credentials, photo, contact information, and profile link are correct.
  2. Open the business card template in the app and use the current version.
  3. Get the cardstock. Preprinted business-card cardstock is located in the right drawer of the kitchen desk.
  4. Use the color Brother printer on the back side of the kitchen desk. The printer can only take one sheet at a time.
  5. Load the cardstock with the QR-code side facing up so the QR code is readable when you look at it.
  6. In the printer settings, set Print Quality to Great instead of Good and Paper Type to Matte Photo Paper. Click OK.
  7. Print one sheet first. Check that your information is correct and everything is properly aligned before printing additional cards.
  8. Once the test sheet looks correct, print additional sheets one at a time.

The preprinted QR code links to the main Next Level Up website. If needed, the cards can also be printed on both sides.

Please use the current app-generated template and do not add a private care-texting number or other personal contact information that is not intended for public use.

If your profile information is incorrect or you have trouble with the template, printer, or alignment, use Need help in the Provider Update to submit a Technology support ticket before continuing. You can attach screenshots. General Next Level Up support: support@nextleveluplcc.com.

SECTION A: Clinical Support Providers (Tier 1)

Applicability and Role Categories

This section applies to employees functioning in Tier 1 Clinical Support roles, which include distinct subcategories with different authorization limits, specifically:

  • Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers (e.g., Bachelor’s-Level Mental Health Counselors)
  • Non-Degree Clinical Support Providers, including:
  • Qualified Behavioral Health Assistants (QBHA)
  • Peer Support Professionals

While all Tier 1 roles operate under supervision and without independent clinical authority, authorization to provide, document, or bill specific services varies by subcategory and is governed by payer rules, program approval, and Practice authorization.

Tier 1 classification alone does not confer uniform service or billing authority.

Role Definition and Purpose

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers expand access to mental health–related services through structured support, skill development, facilitation, engagement, and reinforcement of treatment goals. These roles are designed to complement, not replace, clinical services delivered by Master’s-level or licensed providers.

Tier 1 providers function within Practice-approved programs (including office-based, telehealth, and approved skill development settings) and support client progress through goal-oriented, skill-based interventions aligned with assigned scope and supervision.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Activities

Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers

When explicitly authorized by the Practice and permitted by payer and program rules, Bachelor’s-Level Clinical Support Providers may:

  • Deliver structured individual support services, including H0004 (Behavioral Health Counseling and Therapy) when all authorization, documentation, and supervision requirements are met
  • Facilitate or co-facilitate skill-based, psychoeducational or prevention-focused client groups only within written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Reinforce treatment goals, coping strategies, and behavioral skills established by supervising clinicians
  • Support emotional regulation, social skills, communication, frustration tolerance, and functional improvement
  • Observe, track, and report client progress and engagement
  • Participate in office-based or telehealth services consistent with consent and program scope

Provision of H0004 by Bachelor’s-Level providers does not constitute independent psychotherapy authority and must occur strictly within the approved treatment/service plan and supervision structure.

QBHA and Peer Support Professionals

Qualified Behavioral Health Assistants (QBHA) and Peer Support Professionals may not provide or bill H0004 or any other counseling/therapy codes.

When authorized, these roles may:

  • Deliver non-therapy, skill-based, rehabilitative, outreach, or support services permitted under applicable codes and programs
  • Facilitate or assist with structured client groups only when the program, role and service are authorized under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Support engagement, skill practice, and functional goal reinforcement
  • Provide observation-based feedback to supervising clinicians
  • Participate in approved NLU programming consistent with training and authorization

All services provided by QBHAs and Peer Support Professionals must remain non-clinical in nature and may not be represented as counseling or therapy.

Prohibited Activities and Clinical Limitations (All Tier 1 Roles)

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers may not:

  • Independently diagnose mental health conditions
  • Independently develop, modify, or terminate treatment plans without approval of a licensed and approved clinical supervisor.
  • Provide psychotherapy services reserved for Master’s-level or licensed clinicians
  • Assume service or billing authority based on job title or Tier placement alone
  • Operate outside assigned program scope or supervision
  • Use clinical terminology or representations that exceed authorized scope

Supervision Expectations

All Tier 1 providers are supervised at all times.

  • Supervision requirements apply regardless of experience or tenure
  • Supervision does not confer independent clinical authority
  • Providers must escalate scope questions, safety concerns, or uncertainty through supervisory channels
  • Supervision structure, frequency, and documentation follow SUPERVISION PROCEDURES and the applicable role and training requirements. Required compensable employee work follows Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Documentation Responsibilities

Tier 1 providers are responsible for completing accurate, timely documentation consistent with:

  • Authorized service descriptions
  • Program requirements
  • Coding and billing rules
  • Scope limitations tied to their specific role category

Documentation must remain within the role’s scope and be accurate, timely and complete. Documentation deficiencies may require correction or corrective action. A late note or other documentation concern does not erase earned wages; follow Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Billing and Service Authorization

  • Tier 1 providers may bill services only when explicitly authorized
  • Authorization to bill does not imply clinical independence
  • Providers are responsible for confirming authorization prior to service delivery
  • Billing rules, code eligibility and compensation mappings follow Service-code compensation and authorizations and the individual compensation schedule. Client group services require written NLU program authorization or an express written exception under Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization. Obtain approval before advertising, enrolling or scheduling; a role, credential or saved code mapping does not authorize group delivery.

Do not provide or bill services outside written authorization, scope or payer requirements. Address unauthorized activity through compliance review and correction. Missing preapproval or a denied claim does not erase wages earned for work actually performed; see Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Center-Based and Group Setting Standards

When operating in center-based or group settings, Tier 1 providers must:

  • Adhere to NLU site professionalism, safety, and confidentiality requirements
  • Maintain appropriate professional boundaries
  • Follow escalation and crisis protocols
  • Represent the Practice consistently and professionally

Center-based placement does not expand scope of practice or billing authority.

Relationship to Other Handbook Sections

This section must be read in conjunction with:

  • Workplace Policies and Standards
  • Supervision and Training
  • Role Descriptions and Typical Duties
  • Service-code compensation and authorizations
  • Program-Specific Sections (e.g., Therapy + Tutoring program)

Where conflicts arise, role-specific authorization and scope limitations prevail.

Section A Summary

Tier 1 Clinical Support Providers contribute meaningful, structured services through supervised, skill-based, and program-aligned interventions. While Bachelor’s-Level providers may be authorized to deliver certain counseling services such as H0004, QBHAs and Peer Support Professionals are limited to non-therapy support roles. This section establishes clear internal distinctions to protect clients, staff, and the Practice while ensuring compliant, defensible service delivery.

SECTION C: Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers (Tier 2)

This section applies to employees who hold a Master’s degree in a mental health–related field and are functioning in roles that require advanced clinical knowledge but do not confer independent licensure authority. This includes pre-licensed clinicians actively pursuing licensure and unlicensed Master’s-level providers practicing in roles where licensure is not required or not applicable.

Tier 2 providers deliver clinical and therapeutic services under defined supervision requirements and within Practice-approved scope. Authorization to provide or bill services is determined by credentialing status, supervision, payer requirements, and program approval—not solely by degree attainment or licensure intent.

Role Definition and Professional Standing

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers occupy an intermediate role between training positions and fully licensed clinical practice. These providers are qualified to deliver therapeutic services consistent with their education and training but remain subject to ongoing oversight, supervision, and Practice authorization.

Licensure pursuit may be required, optional, or not applicable depending on role designation, program assignment, and funding source. Regardless of licensure intent, Tier 2 providers do not practice independently.

Scope of Practice and Authorized Clinical Activities

When authorized by the Practice, Tier 2 providers may:

  • Provide authorized individual and family-based therapeutic services aligned with approved treatment or service plans. Client group delivery also requires the written authorization in Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization
  • Conduct clinical assessments and contribute to diagnostic impressions under supervision
  • Develop, implement, and update treatment plans subject to supervisory review
  • Utilize evidence-based and developmentally appropriate clinical interventions consistent with training and supervision
  • Collaborate with families and interdisciplinary teams as permitted by consent
  • Provide services in approved NLU office and telehealth settings as assigned

Tier 2 providers may exercise clinical judgment within their authorized scope, subject to supervision and escalation requirements.

Clinical Authority Limits and Prohibited Activities

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers may not:

  • Practice independently or without required supervision
  • Represent themselves as fully licensed clinicians
  • Provide services outside approved credentialing, payer, or program authorization
  • Ignore or override supervisory direction
  • Assume authority for high-risk clinical decisions without consultation

Independent practice authority is not granted until full licensure and Practice approval are obtained.

Supervision Requirements and Milestones

Tier 2 providers are subject to structured clinical supervision.

  • Supervision frequency, format, and documentation are determined by licensure status, payer rules, and Practice policy
  • Supervisors retain oversight authority and may review, co-sign, or redirect clinical work
  • Providers must escalate safety concerns, ethical dilemmas, scope questions, or complex cases

For pre-licensed providers, supervision may also count toward licensure requirements when conducted by an approved supervisor. Milestone transitions (e.g., increased autonomy, expanded caseloads) are not automatic and require documented approval. For the pre-licensed benefit transition, use the confirmed 60 completed individual/triadic hours plus 40 group opportunities offered in SUPERVISION PROCEDURES. Offered opportunities are not completed licensure hours, and this milestone does not create independent practice authority.

Documentation Responsibilities

Tier 2 providers are responsible for timely, accurate, and clinically appropriate documentation.

Documentation must:

  • Support medical necessity and clinical rationale
  • Accurately reflect services provided and interventions used
  • Align with treatment plans and service authorization
  • Comply with payer, regulatory, and Practice standards

Documentation may be subject to supervisory review, audit, and correction.

Billing and Service Authorization

Pre-Licensed and Unlicensed Master’s-Level Providers may bill services only when authorized by the Practice and permitted by payer and program rules.

  • Billing eligibility depends on credentialing, supervision, and payer requirements
  • Providers must confirm authorization prior to service delivery
  • Billing execution, code authorization and compensation follow Service-code compensation and authorizations, the individual employment agreement and Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Unauthorized or non-compliant billing may result in corrective action.

Center-Based and Interdisciplinary Practice

When practicing in center-based or interdisciplinary environments, Tier 2 providers must:

  • Maintain professional boundaries and role clarity
  • Coordinate appropriately with NLU personnel while adhering to confidentiality requirements

updates.subject: Training leave — separate from sick leave
updates.changed_content:
Training leave — separate from sick leave

Training PTO is paid time earned for approved professional development and training. All hours and service-credit equivalents that qualify for sick-leave accrual also qualify for training accrual, including fee-for-service and salaried employees’ eligible work. The rate is 0.25 training hour per 30 qualifying hours or credits. Use the same documented qualifying basis as sick leave, including applicable clinical-credit equivalents; do not add an equivalent twice.

Training PTO is restricted to approved training and may not be converted to general PTO. It pays at the employee’s applicable sick-leave payment rate for the use date. Required employer training remains paid work even if this benefit has no available balance.

Tracking, cap and ADP handoff

People Operations enters or confirms the current ADP training balance in the app, together with the last completed pay period included in that balance. The app then accrues subsequent eligible periods without counting imported hours again. Staff view their balance and requests in My Payroll. Unused training hours carry forward until used. Accrual pauses at a 20-hour balance cap and resumes after approved use; a cap does not erase an existing balance.

Requesting Training PTO

In My Payroll, choose Training PTO, enter the training date and hours, provide a brief description, enter the training cost and upload a receipt, signup confirmation or proof of participation. People Operations may request further participation documentation. Next Level Up may deny a request if sufficient documentation is not provided. The balance is deducted only when payroll approves the request and applies its payment. Pending or denied requests do not reduce the earned balance. A separate expense reimbursement requires its own approval; reporting a course cost does not automatically create a second payment.

See Continuing Education in the Employee Benefits Overview for additional approval and reimbursement requirements. Training leave is separate from protected sick leave .

Voluntary Training Opportunities

Purpose: Optional professional development opportunities beyond mandatory training.

Eligibility: Open to all employees where relevant to their role.

Attendance: Voluntary and not required.

Compensation: Optional professional development may use approved Training leave — separate from sick leave. Submit the request and supporting documentation in My Payroll. Required employer training remains compensable work even without a Training PTO balance; do not deduct required work from that benefit.

Encouragement: Participation is encouraged but not mandatory.

TRAINING REQUIREMENTS

All new hires are required to complete an orientation program that covers organizational procedures, emergency protocols, and an introduction to our service model. This orientation is essential for all employees to ensure they are well-prepared and aligned with our operational standards. Required onboarding and orientation are paid work under 14. Support Activity.

Individuals enrolled in the Student Training Program should reference the specific training section within the Workplace Handbook dedicated to the Student Training Program. This section outlines additional requirements, expectations, and guidance tailored to their roles and responsibilities within the program.

Similarly, individuals participating in our Therapy + Tutoring program will engage in the training specifically designed for that program. They should refer to the Therapy + Tutoring provider roles and training section of the Workplace Handbook for detailed information on their training requirements, expectations, and guidelines.

It is crucial that all participants and employees review and adhere to the training standards applicable to their respective roles as outlined in the appropriate sections of our Workplace Handbook to ensure consistency and compliance with our organizational policies. Required employer training is paid work even when no Training PTO balance is available. Optional professional development follows Training leave — separate from sick leave.

CONTINUING EDUCATION

See Continuing Education in BENEFITS OVERVIEW and Training leave — separate from sick leave for the current accrual, approval, payment and My Payroll request process. Required employer training remains paid work without using Training PTO.

Our organization is committed to supporting ongoing professional development through continuing education opportunities. All providers are encouraged to engage in relevant training activities that enhance their professional skills and align with our service model.

All employees are encouraged to reference the appropriate section of the Workplace Handbook for detailed guidelines on training requirements and eligibility criteria and their Employment Agreement for more information.

updates.subject: Consistent compensation across funding sources
updates.changed_content:
COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION

Beginning on this amendment’s effective date, I will be compensated at the applicable rates in my individual compensation schedule for the services and duties I perform, regardless of the payment or funding source. This includes insurance, self-pay, grants, iMatter and other externally funded programs or contracts. My compensation is based on the approved service, credits or hours and assigned duties, rather than a percentage of the amount billed, collected or reimbursed. For work covered by this amendment, these terms replace prior funding-specific percentage or revenue-sharing compensation arrangements. Applicable approved differentials and separately stated role or duty rates continue to apply. This change applies prospectively after the required signatures and does not reduce compensation already earned.

Rationale

Funding arrangements have changed over time, and some external contracts have omitted provider-compensation terms or applied them inconsistently. Using each employee’s agreed service and duty rates provides a consistent basis for compensation across programs. Differences in a program’s reimbursement do not create an automatic increase or decrease in the employee’s rate.

For example, a covered 1.00-credit clinical service pays the employee’s agreed per-credit rate whether funded by insurance, a grant or iMatter. It is not paid as 50% of a program’s reimbursement under this amendment. Salaried employees remain subject to their salary agreements. Approved supervision, mentoring and other assigned-duty rates remain governed by the employee’s individual schedule. Any separate group-work compensation must be agreed in writing under the group-review policy.

Payroll must retain the prior arrangement for earlier service dates and apply the new method only from the completed amendment’s prospective effective date. Editing the handbook alone does not change an existing signed agreement or activate a percentage-pay override.

CLIENT POLICIES AND ATTENDANCE

Definitions:

No-Show: A 'no-show' is defined as a failure by the client to appear for a scheduled session without any prior notification to the clinician. This disruption affects scheduling and resource allocation, thereby impacting service delivery to other clients.

Late Cancellation: A 'late cancellation' occurs when a client cancels their scheduled session less than 24 hours before the appointed time. This does not allow sufficient time to reallocate the session slot to another client, thus impacting clinical operations.

Three Missed Sessions Policy:

Clients who miss three sessions for any reason may lose their recurrent session time-slot or be placed on a waitlist at the direction and implementation of the Provider or Facilitator.

This policy is enforced to ensure that our limited client slots are utilized by those who consistently engage in their treatment plans. Providers and Facilitators are encouraged to implement an approach that encourages participation and attendance when three no-show appointments happen for any reason.

Termination should be considered if a client misses three sessions in a row and no communication occurs between the client and the Provider or Facilitator.

With a limited capacity to see clients daily, maintaining efficient scheduling is crucial. Waitlists often occur, and prioritizing clients who can attend regularly helps manage these effectively.

Re-engagement Options:

Clients who no-show or who cancel within the 24 hours time frame should be contacted to discuss their commitment and availability for ongoing services. Providers and Facilitators are encouraged to use the app’s approved communication tools to coordinate alternative times at approved NLU centers or through approved virtual services, based on client availability and regularly scheduled hours.

Providers and Facilitators can offer to reschedule or provide alternative session times as a part of re-engagement efforts, ensuring clients remain engaged in their therapeutic journey even if their regular time slot has been forfeited.

No-Show and Late Cancellation Fees:

Record the appointment as a no-show in the app and document the attendance outcome. The standard no-show fee is $100 for an eligible non-Medicaid client when applicable under the client’s agreement. Submit any fee adjustment through the app’s billing workflow.

Record the cancellation and notice time in the app. The standard late-cancellation fee is $80 for an eligible non-Medicaid client who cancels less than 24 hours before the appointment, subject to the client’s agreement.

These fees are standard but may be adjusted at the clinician's discretion.

Under no circumstances will clients with Medicaid be charged no-show or late cancellation fees. Do not create a missed-appointment charge for a Medicaid client in the app.

Fee Collection and Compensation:

A discretionary missed-appointment benefit follows the employee’s individual agreement and the applicable missed-session policy. A client fee does not automatically create a clinical credit or a revenue share. Work actually performed, including required follow-up, is compensated under the applicable individual service or duty schedule and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION.

Missed-appointment charges not collected within 30 days are referred to billing for handling under Next Level Up’s collection procedures. Collection status may affect a separately agreed discretionary missed-appointment benefit, but it does not cancel wages earned for work actually performed. See Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Documentation and Communication:

Providers and Facilitators are responsible for documenting in the app all instances of no-shows and late cancellations, including any fee adjustments and communications with clients regarding these fees. This documentation helps maintain transparency and accountability within our services.

PERFORMANCE AND EXPECTATIONS

This section outlines professional, clinical, billing, and compliance expectations applicable to all employees providing services on behalf of Next Level Up. Failure to meet these expectations may result in corrective action in accordance with Practice policies.

Clinical Service Standards

A Clinical Session or Clinical Service is considered properly rendered only when:

  • The service is actually delivered;
  • The service is within the employee’s scope of practice, training, and credentialing;
  • Required authorizations are obtained when applicable; and
  • Clinical documentation is completed in accordance with Practice standards.

Administrative, concierge, subscription, or other payments to Next Level Up do not create an automatic employee revenue share. Employees are paid for the services and assigned duties they actually perform under their individual compensation schedule and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION. Required administrative work remains compensable under Actual time, support activities and corrections.

Documentation Standards

Timely, accurate, and complete clinical documentation is a fundamental professional responsibility.

Documentation must be completed in accordance with Practice standards and applicable laws.

Documentation that is late, incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent with services rendered may render a service Deficient.

Documentation timeliness and payroll deadlines follow TIMEKEEPING, COMPENSATION, AND PAYROLL COMPLIANCE. Documentation and approval concerns are handled separately from paying for work performed.

Deficient Services

Deficient Services include, but are not limited to, services that:

  • Are not delivered as scheduled or documented as delivered;
  • Are inadequately, inaccurately, or untimely documented;
  • Are provided in violation of third-party payor rules, applicable laws, or ethical standards;
  • Are conducted outside of required licensure, credentialing, or authorization parameters; or
  • Result in denial, recoupment, or retraction of payment due to provider-controlled noncompliance.

Deficient Services may result in corrective action, remediation, review of billing privileges, client reassignment, or other appropriate compliance action. Correct inaccurate records and payment errors through the designated review process. A late note, missing preapproval, or denied claim does not erase earned wages; Actual time, support activities and corrections governs compensation for actual work.

Billing and Insurance Compliance

Employees are responsible for complying with all billing, insurance, and payor requirements applicable to the services they provide.

Credentialing and Licensure

Employees must maintain required licensure and credentialing to bill insurance.

Delays or failures attributable to the employee that prevent insurance billing may result in client transition to self-pay or reassignment.

The Practice reserves the right to inform clients of credentialing limitations impacting billing.

Insurance Denials and Recoupment

If a payer denies or retracts payment because of inadequate services or documentation, address the billing and compliance issue through review and correction. A payer denial does not automatically deny, reduce, or recoup employee compensation already earned. Apply Actual time, support activities and corrections and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION.

Repeated billing deficiencies may result in loss of insurance billing privileges.

Medicaid-Specific Rules

Medicaid clients may never be charged self-pay rates.

If a provider is unable to bill Medicaid due to noncompliance, services must be provided pro-bono or clients must be transferred for continuity of care.

Providers who fall out of compliance may be restricted or revoked from serving Medicaid clients until compliance is restored.

Self-Pay Services

Clients who are uninsured, elect not to use insurance, receive services not covered by insurance, or lack a billable diagnosis may be billed at self-pay rates in accordance with Practice policy.

All self-pay clients are billed at Practice minimum rates unless otherwise approved.

Required self-pay and No Surprises Act forms must be completed prior to billing.

Non-billable diagnoses must be handled as self-pay unless otherwise specified by policy.

Reduced Rates (Sliding Scale)

Reduced rates may be approved on a case-by-case basis to support access to care.

Requests must be initiated through the Support Team and approved by appropriate leadership.

Reduced rates must be client-initiated due to financial hardship and must contribute meaningfully to care (e.g., increased frequency or duration).

An approved reduction in a client’s rate does not automatically reduce the employee’s compensation. Covered services and duties use the individual compensation schedule under COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION; changes apply prospectively with the required notice and agreement.

Reduced rates most commonly apply to 90837 services, with approved rates set by policy.

Billing protocols must be followed as outlined by the Administrative Team.

Pro-Bono Services

Pro-bono services may be approved to support clients experiencing financial hardship.

Approval must be obtained prior to initiation.

Pro-bono describes the charge to the client. Approved work performed by an employee remains compensated under the applicable individual service or duty rate and COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION. No client charge or reimbursement does not make compensable employee work unpaid.

Pro-bono services may apply to any service offered by the provider.

Sessions must be properly identified and documented in the app in accordance with Practice protocols.

Professional Conduct and Ethics

Employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of professional and ethical conduct, including compliance with:

  • The ACA Code of Ethics;
  • HIPAA and confidentiality requirements; and
  • All applicable laws and regulations.

Ethical or legal concerns must be reported promptly to Compliance. Failure to report or address known concerns may result in corrective action.

Auditing and Oversight

Next Level Up conducts periodic review and auditing of clinical documentation and services, including through third-party compliance partners.

Findings of significant noncompliance or unethical conduct may result in remediation, corrective action, or further disciplinary measures as outlined in the Remediation section of this Handbook.

Health Insurance — employee-only employer contribution

Basis of the agency contribution

For eligible employees enrolled in agency-sponsored health insurance, the agency contribution is based on the premium for employee-only coverage and the contribution percentage or amount applicable to the employee’s benefit eligibility. Enrollment in employee-plus-spouse, employee-plus-child or family coverage does not increase the agency contribution. The agency does not contribute toward the additional cost of dependent coverage.

Employee responsibility and dependent enrollment

The employee pays the portion of the employee-only premium not covered by the agency contribution, plus the full additional premium for enrolled dependents. Eligible dependents may still enroll when permitted by the plan; this policy limits the agency’s premium contribution and does not exclude dependents from coverage. It does not promise payment of the employee’s full premium.

Where to review your benefit

People Operations maintains the employee-only premium used to calculate the contribution, separately from any additional dependent premium. Contact People Operations if the displayed premium includes family coverage or differs from the carrier’s employee-only amount.

The governing plan documents and applicable law control coverage, eligibility, enrollment and administration. Any change affecting an existing contribution arrangement must be applied prospectively with required notice and any required agreement; this handbook update does not itself change payroll deductions or an existing signed agreement.

updates.subject: Therapy + Tutoring: groups, 50/50 visits and separate service records
updates.changed_content:
THERAPY + TUTORING · COGNITIVE & EMOTIONAL ENRICHMENT

Next Level Up coordinates academic instruction, emotional skill development and counseling for children and teens whose learning and emotional needs overlap. An individualized plan identifies the barriers, goals, appropriate services, qualified providers and measures of progress.

Programs operate at approved NLU locations or through approved virtual services. Select the service that meets the client’s needs; combining services never changes the scope or funding rules for either component.

Program overview and core interventions

The program connects personalized learning support with emotional regulation, coping, attention, organization, persistence and confidence. Academic work may focus on reading, writing, mathematics, study strategies and homework routines. Clinical counseling addresses assessed treatment needs through an individualized treatment plan.

Group skills, individual counseling and tutoring are distinct services within a coordinated plan. An activity is classified by what is actually delivered and by the provider’s role, rather than by the program name or the presence of a learning task.

Small-group skills: scheduling and attendance

Schedule at least three clients for a small-group skills session. At least two must attend for it to proceed as a group. Plan developmentally appropriate skill practice and document each participant’s attendance, response and progress toward their own goals.

If one client attends, reschedule or offer a separately agreed self-pay individual skills service. Do not substitute an insurance claim for individual skills or bill for people who did not attend. Individual skills services are not currently provided through insurance. See Group services and Therapy + Tutoring authorization.

The 50/50 visit: counseling and tutoring

A planned 50/50 visit reserves one appointment for up to 30 minutes of counseling and up to 30 minutes of self-pay tutoring. These are sequential, separately identifiable service periods. The same qualified provider may deliver both only when authorized for each role; otherwise the plan identifies the responsible provider for each portion.

Record the actual start and end of each portion. The scheduled split is a planning target, not proof that either service occurred. Tutoring, breaks, transition time and counseling must not be counted as the same billable minutes. Do not extend or fabricate a clinical service merely to fill the booking.

H0004 is the requested counseling code, subject to current payer, setting, provider, supervision and treatment-plan eligibility. It must not be used to relabel academic tutoring or individual skills services. Counseling and tutoring each need their own approved funding and compensation treatment.

Combined booking rollout

The combined booking workflow is being prepared. Until NLU announces that it is available, use the app’s existing scheduling, documentation and timekeeping workflows and have Billing reconcile the two service portions. Do not assume a booking automatically creates correct insurance, tutoring-charge or payroll entries.

Documentation, billing and provider time

One workflow, distinct service records

Complete the visit through one coordinated workflow with a counseling section and a short tutoring section. Reuse verified client, appointment, provider and date information. The counseling record identifies the treatment goal, intervention, response, plan, actual clinical time and required signature or co-signature. The tutoring record identifies the learning goal, instructional work, progress and actual tutoring time.

Only the clinical portion supports an insurance claim. The self-pay tutoring portion is recorded separately for the family’s agreed charges. Academic notes do not substitute for a clinical note, and tutoring details are not copied into a payer-facing clinical export unless relevant and appropriate. Each component retains its own service identity, timing, provider and audit trail.

Provider compensation

Record actual counseling and tutoring time separately, linked to the same visit. Apply the employee’s approved service mappings and written rates. Do not count an entire blended booking as counseling, duplicate the same work in two payroll claims, or infer a tutoring rate from H0004. The shared compensation policy continues to apply, including applicable indirect allowances and payment for all compensable work; client payment or a denied insurance claim does not erase earned wages.

Before charging or submitting

Verify the actual service, eligibility, code, units, modifiers, provider enrollment, supervision and payer rules for the date of service. A reserved 30-minute slot is not automatically a two-unit claim. Billing must confirm the configured rule before releasing output.

Verify whether a service is genuinely noncovered before offering a Medicaid member self-pay. Use a specific written payment agreement before the noncovered service, identifying the service and charge. A denied or improperly authorized covered service must not be automatically transferred to the family.

Reference: HCPF January 2026 Provider Bulletin — Member Billing. Current plan-specific rules and NLU’s approved fee schedule govern the actual billing setup.

Provider roles and program training

Staff work within their verified credentials, approved service scope and assigned supervision. Tutors deliver academic instruction; a tutoring assignment does not authorize counseling, diagnosis or insurance billing. Clinical providers deliver counseling only when their credentials, supervision and NLU authorization permit it.

Program orientation covers individualized learning and treatment goals, separation of services and time, skills-group attendance rules, family communication, site safety, documentation and escalation. Assigned employee training is paid work under the shared compensation policy. Intern participation follows the Student Training Program.
